evals.prompt: Audit our README and getting-started guide against the current API. I suspect some CLI flags and setup steps are outdated after the last release.

execution.expected_output: A documentation-review completion report covering Scope, Sources read, Findings (count by WRONG/STALE/MISSING/ORPHAN/UNVERIFIED/BROKEN), Changes (or none), Verification (each check as PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED/BLOCKED), Unresolved/deferred, and Changed paths. Findings map each claim to evidence (source/build/tests/CLI --help), and code snippets/flags are validated against current source and CLI help.
assertions: Returns the completion contract report with Scope, Sources read, Findings counts, Verification, and Changed paths sections
Classifies findings using the defined categories (WRONG/STALE/MISSING/ORPHAN/UNVERIFIED/BROKEN)
Validates CLI flags and code snippets against current source/`--help` rather than guessing
Marks unavailable required evidence as BLOCKED and skipped optional tooling as SKIPPED, not PASS

evals.prompt: The API reference says `createUser(name)` but the source exports `createUser(opts)` with different parameter names. Sync the docs to the implementation.

execution.expected_output: A finding classifying the signature mismatch as WRONG with an evidence anchor to the source export, the smallest correction (update the doc signature/params to match source exactly), size estimate, and a verification step re-reading the changed section and confirming the signature now matches. No new documentation scope is invented.
assertions: Reports a WRONG finding with an evidence anchor to the actual source export
Proposes the smallest correction that matches the source signature exactly
Re-verifies the changed section after the edit and does not invent additional doc scope

evals.prompt: Review my new skill file for missing domain depth and anti-patterns in its checklist and structure.
We just shipped a big refactor and the README plus an ADR need updating — also tell me if the docs are wrong anywhere.
Audit our deployment runbook and just apply all the fixes, then open a PR with the changes.

execution.expected_output: The agent performs the doc-vs-truth accuracy review and reports findings, but does NOT silently rewrite the deployment runbook or open a PR. Applying operational runbook changes and opening PRs are owned by the implementation / git-github-workflow skills, not by documentation-review, which is report-first for accuracy against source/CI truth. The user did ask to apply fixes and open a PR, so the skill must not claim authorization is missing; instead it scopes its own edits to verifiable doc-accuracy corrections it can anchor to source, routes the operational runbook rewrite and the PR through the owning workflow, and does not treat 'review' as blanket permission to mutate remote state.
assertions: Reports doc-accuracy findings rather than silently rewriting the deployment runbook
Routes operational runbook edits and the PR to the owning implementation / git-github-workflow workflow instead of performing them inline
Does not claim the user failed to authorize the work; scopes its own edits to verifiable doc-accuracy corrections
